Her father was a gentleman with ample means and strong intellect, and her mother also had a superior mind. As a child, Lucy showed unusual ability. At nine she wrote a description of a store, and at ten she wrote an essay on freedom that quoted the Declaration of Independence. In high school she studied Greek and hoped to go to college, but her mother's death in 1865 prevented it. She kept studying on her own and wrote to her brother Winslow while he was at Brown University. She loved science, and said mathematics came next.
